doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Benny Goodman and first US jobs
title: Goodman tour details and learning from Dick Hyman
summary: A six-week tour mostly in Italy and Scandinavia; he learned harmony from Dick Hyman and recalls Roy Eldridge.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So that was your first time… a long contract with American musicians, yes?

Yes, I was with Benny Goodman. It was a six weeks tour, I think. We played a lot in Italy. We played a lot in Rome. We were staying in Rome and working around it, you know. And in Belgium, two, three dates. In France and in Sweden, Scandinavia, you know.
And this experience working with the American musicians, did it…
…change your sound or change your concepts or…?

Yes and no. I learned a lot harmonically from Dick Hyman. He was already, he had already played on the Street, you know. He was up to all that was needed for the Street, for the bebop on the Street. And I learned a lot from him.
How about Roy Eldridge’s sound? I mean, my gosh. [laughs]
I know, I knew him from in the jazz, you know.
